coursework.summary: AI use depends on the instructor and assignment. Penn has no standardized student AI-use policy; without other guidance, treat AI as assistance from another person. Wharton Academy examples apply only to that program and require instructor permission.

exams.summary: No uniform university-wide AI exam permission was established. Follow the specific assessment rules; Wharton Academy expressly prohibits AI cheating in its exams and tests. Tool availability grants no exam permission.

ai_disclosure.summary: Community guidance directs transparency and disclosure, while stating it is not a final policy. Instructors may impose specific citation/disclosure requirements; Wharton Academy treats uncredited AI work as plagiarism.

privacy_data_entry.summary: Protect student, patient and research data. Unlicensed tools must not receive identifiable student information; student work requires permission even if anonymized. Do not require personal information or IP in unlicensed tools. Licensed-tool data conditions differ.

approved_tools.summary: Institutional tools have product-specific audience, account, cost and data conditions. PennChat requires PennKey and campus/VPN access; verify current entitlements with IT. Tool access is separate from assessment permission.

research_guidance.summary: Consult department leadership and discipline publication standards about AI authorship. Research-participant data requires appropriate consent and prior IRB approval; data/IP safeguards and Penn Center for Innovation consultation apply.

academic_integrity.summary: Course rules determine unauthorized AI assistance. Wharton Academy has its own restrictions. CETLI advises discussing suspected misuse with students and consulting CSA; it says not to upload work into AI detectors and rejects their accuracy as misconduct evidence. Formal hearing/appeal procedures remain a gap.

teaching_guidance.summary: Instructors set and communicate course/assignment expectations. Unlicensed tools must not require student personal information or IP; consider licensed tools for mandatory coursework. Investigate suspected misuse through conversation and appropriate consultation.

security_procurement.summary: Moderate/high-risk data involves Privacy Office review and Information Security consultation coordinated by Procurement; IP involves Penn Center for Innovation. University business AI processes should have oversight and output verification.

named_ai_services.summary: Named tools have different access and data conditions; directory inclusion is not course or examination approval.

policy_presence.summary: Community guidance, course-specific rules and program policies coexist; no standardized university-wide student AI-use policy is established.
